lesson.title: Public benefits and emergency services
lesson.summary: Recognise public-assistance eligibility and emergency triage/dispatch decisions.

prerequisites.reason: Public assistance is examined as a listed-use match rather than a product classification. Emergency-service functions are examined as listed-use matches rather than product classifications.

blocks: The **public-benefits use** covers AI used by or on behalf of public authorities to evaluate eligibility for essential public assistance benefits or services, including healthcare, and to grant, reduce, revoke or reclaim them.

A fictional municipal Northbridge service evaluates applications for essential assistance. Identify the public-authority connection and the particular decision; not all public-sector administration performs this function.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 5(a), 5(d); Article 6(2), 6(3)

blocks: The **emergency-triage use** includes evaluating/classifying emergency calls, dispatching or prioritising emergency first response, including police, firefighters and medical aid, and emergency healthcare patient triage.
A tool sorting callers by urgency directly raises the listed comparison. A tool organising an unrelated office rota has different facts.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 5(a), 5(d); Article 6(2), 6(3)

blocks: Changed case: a benefits assistant only provides office hours. It later recommends whether an applicant's entitlement should be withdrawn. That is a substantial change in the intended decision function.
Changed case: a call transcription tool also assigns priority. Record the added evaluation instead of treating it as mere text conversion.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 5(a), 5(d); Article 6(2), 6(3)

blocks: Northbridge's packet records actor, person affected, decision type, input, output and influence. The point identifies the classification route; it does not supply a lawful basis under every benefits, health or data-protection rule.
Apply the remaining paragraph 3, profiling, scope and timing checks. Keep a missing decision-use fact explicit rather than assuming outputs have no effect.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 5(a), 5(d); Article 6(2), 6(3)
